prompt_text: {Subjects} provides vocabulary for the subjects appearing in the scene. Use relevant entries to inspire subject choices or appearances without replacing subjects explicitly requested by the user.
{Actions} provides vocabulary for actions and events. Use relevant entries to inspire what subjects do while preserving any action already specified by the user.
{Spaces} provides vocabulary describing where the action takes place. Use relevant entries as possible locations or environmental inspiration.
{Objects} provides vocabulary for physical objects. Objects can be used by subjects, held by subjects, worn where appropriate, interacted with, or included in the background.

{Positions & Poses} provides vocabulary for how subjects are positioned or posed. Apply relevant entries to the appropriate subjects while keeping their bodies, actions, and interactions physically coherent.
{Expressions} provides vocabulary for facial expressions and visible reactions. Apply relevant expressions to appropriate subjects.
{Clothing} provides vocabulary for outfits and garments. Apply relevant entries to appropriate subjects while respecting their appearance and the user request.

{Mood & Tone} provides vocabulary for the overall emotional atmosphere or attitude of the scene. Use relevant entries to influence how the scene feels without unnecessarily changing the requested action.
{Lighting} provides vocabulary for illumination, lighting conditions, and light sources. Use relevant entries to establish coherent scene lighting.
{Camera & Composition} provides vocabulary for shot types, camera angles, framing, and viewpoints. Use relevant entries to compose the scene while keeping required subjects and actions visible.
{Effects & Atmosphere} provides vocabulary for visible environmental, atmospheric, magical, and cinematic effects. Use relevant entries when they contribute naturally to the scene.
